meta.title: Ten Days That Shook the World: places, factions and movements in Reed's Petrograd

text.edition: Project Gutenberg #3076 (Norman Wolcott, with corrections by Andrew Sly and Stefan Malte Schumacher; updated 3 March 2021). Its graphics are keyed to the pages of the original edition.

pdf.note: calibre 9.16.0, generated 2026-10-21, 309 pages. p is the PDF page index (the printed page number is one lower). Footnotes are moved to the end of each chapter; some photo captions are the editors', not Reed's.

ref.q: I have adopted in this book our Calendar throughout, instead of the former Russian Calendar, which was thirteen days earlier.

calendar.note: Reed keeps to New Style in his narrative, but the documents he prints, and a few of his own lines, use Old Style. Each event says which in cal.

petrograd.basis: Pulkovo mean time (UTC+2:01:19) plus the 1917 summer hour, in force from 1 July until Decree No. 142 of December 1917. Assumes Reed's times are local clock times; he never says.

moscow.basis: tzdb Europe/Moscow for 1917 (2:31:19) plus the summer hour.

blocs.soviet: For the insurrection and Soviet power: the Bolsheviki, the Left SRs, the Military Revolutionary Committee, the Red Guards, most of the garrison and the fleet.
blocs.government: The Provisional Government and those who fought for it: its ministers and staff, the yunker schools, Krasnov's Cossacks, the Women's Battalion.
blocs.opposition: Against the insurrection without being the deposed government: the City Duma, the Committee for Salvation, the Mensheviki and SRs, the Cadets, the old Tsay-ee-kah and Peasants' Executive.
blocs.neutral: Declared neutral or split: the Petrograd Cossacks, Vikzhel, several regiments.

meta.note: A seed dataset for a 3D map of Reed's book, not of the revolution. It follows Reed authoritatively: what he says happened, where, when, and how he knew it.
